notes: ACCESS: clean. probe.fetch() returned HTTP 200 on every request across rotating fingerprints (safari18_0_ios, safari18_0, safari17_2_ios, chrome131); no Akamai/DataDome/Cloudflare interstitial, no 403, no 429, no reader prefix or alternate profile set needed. Pages are large (0.4-2.6 MB of server-rendered React) but fully rendered server-side, so no browser automation and no API host were needed - which matters, because robots forbids /api/*. Single host throughout (www.westwing.de serves pages and sitemaps), so no second robots.txt was owed. ROBOTS - READ CAREFULLY, THIS SITE NAMES CLAUDE: https://www.westwing.de/robots.txt was fetched FIRST (HTTP 200, safari18_0_ios) before any other request. It has four groups. The fourth is a shared AI-agent group whose user-agent list includes 'User-agent: ClaudeBot', 'User-agent: Claude-Web' and 'User-agent: anthropic-ai' (alongside GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, Amazonbot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, CCBot, FacebookBot, Meta-ExternalAgent, Bytespider, TikTokBot, YouBot, FriendlyCrawler, OpenAI-Webcrawler, DataForSEObot, Diffbot, AI2Bot, NeevaAI). This group is the most specific one matching us, so it governs. It is NOT a blanket opt-out: it contains no 'Disallow: /'. Its directives are verbatim 'Allow: /llms.txt', 'Allow: /new-products/$', 'Allow: /customer/invitation/create/', 'Allow: /*/customer/invitation/create/', then 'Disallow: /all-products', 'Disallow: /p/s/*', 'Disallow: /customer*', 'Disallow: *--*', 'Disallow: /*?*q=*', 'Disallow: *?c=', 'Disallow: *&c=', 'Disallow: /sso/*', 'Disallow: /c/*', 'Disallow: /products/*', 'Disallow: /collections/*', 'Disallow: /api/*' - byte-identical to the generic '*' group apart from the extra 'Allow: /llms.txt'. So this is a uniform site-wide ruleset, not a Claude-targeted exclusion, and no Disallow in it covers the paths needed here. CRITICALLY, Westwing's category listing pages do NOT live under /c/, /collections/ or /products/: they are bare first-level slugs (/badezimmer-deko/, /seifenspender/, /badmoebel/ ...), which the site's own sitemap-categories.xml confirms for all 602 category URLs - zero of them contain '/c/'. Every URL requested this session was such a bare slug, or /sitemap.xml, or /sitemap-categories.xml, none of which is disallowed. Nothing disallowed was touched: no '--' URL was requested (checked - zero of the 602 category URLs contain '--'), no ?q= search, no ?c= or &c= parameter, no /api/, /products/, /collections/, /c/, /all-products, /p/s/, /customer or /sso path. No Crawl-delay is declared in any group; probe.py's 2 s per-host gap was kept. Product counts were therefore taken from rendered HTML only - the /api/ route was never used, precisely because it is disallowed. TREE: taken from the site's own navigation, three independent sources cross-checked. (1) The homepage embeds the full mega-menu in its React flight payload; 308 distinct labelled label->href pairs were extracted verbatim, giving the departments Möbel, Aufbewahrung, Accessoires, Leuchten, Teppiche, Textilien, Geschirr-Serien/Küche, Kinder, Gartenmöbel, Geschenke, Shop by Room, Marken. (2) Every PLP renders a 'plp-category-chips' strip naming its parent ('Alle <Parent>') and all its siblings, which is the site's own machine-readable category tree; it was harvested on each page visited and is what fixed each node's parent. (3) https://www.westwing.de/sitemap.xml -> https://www.westwing.de/sitemap-categories.xml (HTTP 200, 602 category URLs), regex-scanned for bad|bath|dusch|wanne|wc|toilette|waschbecken|waschtisch|armatur|sanitaer|spiegel|handtuch|seife|wasch, which recovered nodes the mega-menu truncates - /badmoebel/, /shower-curtains/, /decorative-mirrors-1/, /babyhandtuecher/, /seifen-cremes/, /seifenspender/, /bademaentel/, /badezimmerteppiche/, /antirutschmatten/. The bathroom branch that results is: Accessoires > Badaccessoires (/badezimmer-deko/, H1 'Badaccessoires', 420) with exactly nine children in the site's own chip order - Seifen & Cremes 53, Seifenspender & -schalen 87, Zahnputzbecher 42, Badaufbewahrung 71, Wäschekörbe 59, Kosmetikeimer 56, Toilettenbürsten 60, Toilettenpapierhalter 39, Handtuchhalter 36. Eight of the nine are recorded; Seifen & Cremes is routed out (consumable soaps and washing-up liquid). Alongside it sit Möbel > Schränke > Badschränke and Möbel > Regale > Badregale (both already in Furniture.xlsx), Accessoires > Spiegel > Kosmetikspiegel / Wandspiegel / Ganzkörperspiegel (all three already in Final.xlsx), Textilien > Badtextilien and its three children, plus Bademäntel, Shower curtains, Babyhandtücher and Teppiche > Nach Raum > Badezimmer, all routed to Textile. Westwing is a design/home-decor retailer: it sells NO sanitaryware, taps, basins, WCs, baths, showers or enclosures - the sitemap sweep for waschbecken|waschtisch|armatur|dusch|wanne|wc|sanitaer returned nothing beyond the nodes above, so those parts of rules 4-8 have no counterpart here and nothing was skipped. WÄSCHEKÖRBE JUDGEMENT: it is reachable by two paths - the mega-menu lists it under Aufbewahrung, but the site's own PLP chip strip gives its parent as 'Alle Badaccessoires' (/badezimmer-deko/) and it is also a chip of the Shop-by-Room Badezimmer hub. Two of the three site-declared placements are bathroom, so rule 12 ('Baskets ... include when site presents it under Bathroom; hierarchy decides') puts it in Bathroom, recorded once under the single canonical URL (rule 28). QTY: every figure is the listing page's OWN rendered German total, read from two places on the same page - the toolbar line '<N> Produkte' and the footer line '<shown> von <N> Produkten werden angezeigt' - which agreed on every node. On the four nodes large enough to paginate the two differ as expected (Badaccessoires '420 Produkte' / '120 von 420', Badtextilien '429 Produkte' / '120 von 429', Handtücher '225' / '120 von 225', Badmöbel '485' / '120 von 485'), proving the page size is 120 and that the toolbar number is a true paginated total, not a page-size artifact; on every recorded leaf the totals are below 120 and the footer reads 'N von N'. A third independent source agrees where the page embeds it: the server-rendered Algolia block carries \"nbHits\",485 on /badmoebel/ and 429 on /badtextilien/, matching the rendered strings exactly. Counts discriminate strongly (1, 7, 12, 16, 18, 33, 36, 37, 39, 42, 50, 53, 56, 59, 60, 71, 87, 130, 139, 206, 225, 228, 420, 429, 485), so no site-wide constant is in play. Every recorded page's H1 and BreadcrumbList were checked against the node requested and matched (Seifenspender & -schalen, Zahnputzbecher, Badaufbewahrung, Wäschekörbe, Kosmetikeimer, Toilettenbürsten, Toilettenpapierhalter, Handtuchhalter). Nothing was estimated, no parent number was reused for a child, and no siblings were summed - note the nine Badaccessoires children total 503 against a parent of 420, i.e. they genuinely overlap, which is exactly why only children are recorded and the parent is a blank grouping row. DUPLICATE-URL FAMILIES RESOLVED: Westwing serves room-scoped clones of the same categories under '-2'/'-3' handles (/seifenspender-2/ 87 = /seifenspender/ 87, /handtuchhalter-2/ 36 = /handtuchhalter/ 36, /bad-aufbewahrung-2/ 71 = /bad-aufbewahrung/ 71, /waeschekoerbe-waeschetaschen-2/ 59 = /waeschekoerbe-waeschetaschen/ 59). Each pair was fetched and compared; the plain handle is the one carrying <link rel=canonical> and BreadcrumbList JSON-LD while the '-2' twin carries neither, so the plain handle is recorded and the twin discarded (rule 28). The two exceptions are documented in review[]: /badschraenke-2/ (60 vs 36) and /badezimmer-deko-2/ (206 vs 420), which are genuinely different scoped sets rather than clones. DEDUP: dedup.already_extracted() was run on all 29 candidate and control URLs before anything was recorded. Four are exact hits and none of them is in rows[] - /badschraenke (Furniture.xlsx 'Bathroom Cabinets'), /badregale (Furniture.xlsx 'Bathroom Shelving'), /schminkspiegel (Final.xlsx 'Vanity Mirrors'), /wandspiegel (Final.xlsx 'Wall Mirrors'), /ganzkoerperspiegel (Final.xlsx 'Full-Length Mirrors').
